epics.title: Model Viewer — owner site
epics.description:
A 3D model gallery and viewer on owner.sparktobloom.com, so Daniel can pan, tilt and zoom over a model Skippy is working on — from a phone, without installing anything — and so both of them can be provably looking at the same feature. Requirements agreed 2026-09-22 and revised the same evening after the adversarial review.

Shape: two halves, because the thing that can convert CAD and the thing that serves the web page cannot be the same process. The worker runs on the workstation as a user systemd unit, where freecadcmd already lives, and owns every derived artifact — for each model file it writes a normalised binary STL, a thumbnail PNG and a small record of what happened, into a cache directory outside the models tree, and it watches the tree and rebuilds what changes. The site runs in owner-app and is a pure reader: it converts nothing, renders nothing, holds no CAD stack, and reads the cache, serves bytes and keeps the camera state, so a wedged conversion cannot stall a page. The browser always loads a normalised binary STL whatever the source format was — one loader, no text parsing, and no 179 MB OBJ opened in phone Safari.

Out of scope for this build: measurement, meaning click two vertices or edges and get a distance, named as the likely next feature; a slicer pane driving OrcaSlicer beside the model view with auto-orient, face picking, walls and infill, tree supports and the sliced render; and exploded views, several models on screen at once, print-bed-for-scale, colour by wall thickness, and any upload, edit or delete from the browser.
epics.requirements: Thirty-six numbered requirements, carried as stories across the features below. The gallery lists every model under the models tree as cards with a picture, a name and a size, browsable by folder. The 3D view orbits, pans and zooms by mouse and by touch, opens immediately with a loading percentage, and cancels cleanly on back. Every model is prebuilt before Daniel ever opens the gallery, and a later addition is picked up within seconds. A model is never served half-built. Every distinct failure is stated distinctly and the states are distinguishable on one listing. Skippy can push a camera and a marker, read back where Daniel is looking, and is never handed his own push as Daniel's answer. A section plane cuts the model open. A rebuilt model swaps in with the camera held. Only Daniel sees any of it, Skippy reaches it with his own token, every route is covered including the bytes routes, no token configured admits no bearer including an empty one, an invalid credential is a 401 rather than a 500, nothing outside the models directory and the cache is reachable including via a symlink, a filename is data rather than syntax, opening a gallery costs one auth call rather than one per card, and nothing under the models directory is ever written. Every folder has its own address at any depth with an open model as a query parameter, each navigation adds exactly one history entry, back from a direct arrival leaves the section, reloading restores what was on screen, the back button and section slider belong to the 3D view alone, and a bad address corrects itself with a note while a missing or unreadable models directory says so and keeps the address because the remedy is a mount.
epics.acceptance_criteria: The adversarial review changed the design in six ways worth recording, because the reasoning matters more than the edit. Conversion cannot live in owner-app: the image is python:3.12-slim with six pure-Python packages, so tests calling host freecadcmd would have gone green while all 86 CAD files showed conversion-failed in production — hence the worker. Torn reads were the worst finding, twice: a mesh read while being written parses as a valid STL with geometry missing, and the old cache rule would have kept it forever; a source read while Skippy rebuilds it does the same; both render fine and are wrong, which is the exact opposite of the one thing this page exists to do. Skippy reading his own push back as Daniel's answer was the subtlest — one slot, two writers, and a confident wrong answer. Eleven of the original twenty-one tests passed against the bug they named, the worst being that 'no token configured authorizes nobody' only failed for an empty presented bearer, which the original test never sent. Sizes were wrong: the largest file is a 326 MB STEP rather than the 105 MB vase, and there is also a 179 MB OBJ, which is why the browser now always gets a normalised binary mesh. And the tree bites: one uppercase .STL, two basename collisions, three files sharing one stem, an apostrophe in a directory name, and a restrictive mode on the root itself.
epics.qa_tests: Twenty-seven tests, each naming what it breaks against — derived against the test standard, then rewritten after refute-tests proved eleven of the first twenty-one would pass against the bug they named. Five behaviours are verified live at ship time rather than by the suite, because they have no assertable surface in pytest: tapping a card and orbiting by mouse and touch; the progress bar tracking a real download and the cancel returning immediately; a pushed camera actually moving Daniel's view with the marker visible; the section plane cutting the solid; and a rebuilt model swapping in with the camera held while polling stops on a hidden tab. One requirement is deliberately untested: 'nothing under the models directory is written' is the absence of write routes plus a read-only mount, and per the standard a removal earns no test that it is gone.

features.title: The worker — every derived artifact
features.description: A user systemd unit on the workstation, where freecadcmd lives. It owns the cache: a normalised binary STL, a thumbnail PNG and a record of what happened per model, written outside the models tree. It watches and rebuilds.
features.requirements: R10: every model file already has its picture and viewable mesh built before Daniel opens the gallery, whatever the source format. R11: a model added or rebuilt later is picked up on its own within seconds, and its card says building until ready. R12: whatever the source format, what the browser loads is a mesh of that model — STEP and FreeCAD documents are not a second class of file, and the only observable difference is that a brand-new one spends a few seconds building. R13: a model is never served half-built — a mesh still being written is not offered, and a source still being written is not read. R14: every distinct failure is stated distinctly and the five states are distinguishable on one listing: could not convert, could not be read, could not be pictured, still building, and a conversion that hung and was abandoned. R28: a filename cannot change what the converter does — spaces, apostrophes and nine levels of nesting are data, never syntax. R30: nothing under the models directory is ever written, moved or deleted; the mount is read-only.
features.acceptance_criteria: A wedged conversion cannot stall a page, because the site holds no CAD stack at all.
features.qa_tests: The conversion tests assert against the real part's geometry rather than a triangle count, because a unit cube passes a count assertion and fails a bounding-box one. The torn-read tests are the ones the review called the worst finding: a mesh read mid-write parses as valid STL with geometry missing.

stories.title: Prebuild the whole tree before first visit
stories.description: R10 and R12. Every model ends with a mesh, a thumbnail and a ready state.
stories.requirements: All formats, not only native meshes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A listing after the pass reports nothing pending.
stories.qa_tests: Four models in three formats all end ready. Breaks if the pass handles only native meshes, or stops at the first failure.

stories.title: Convert a real STEP to that STEP's geometry
stories.description: R12. The assertion is a bounding box matching the known dimensions of a committed real part, to a tolerance.
stories.requirements: The converter must honour its input.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The mesh is that part.
stories.qa_tests: gang-box-2g.step converts to a mesh whose bounding box matches the part. Breaks if the converter ignores its input — a unit cube passes a triangle-count assertion and fails this one.

stories.title: Convert a real FreeCAD document to that document's geometry
stories.description: R12. Same bounding-box assertion against a committed .FCStd fixture.
stories.requirements: The FCStd path exercised on its own.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The mesh is that document.
stories.qa_tests: Breaks if the FCStd path is wired to the STEP path and never exercised.

stories.title: Render a thumbnail that is a picture of its own model
stories.description: R3 and R10.
stories.requirements: Distinct per model, and not blank.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Two models produce different pictures.
stories.qa_tests: Two models' thumbnails differ in bytes and each contains more than one distinct pixel value. Breaks if the renderer emits a blank square, or the same square for every input.

stories.title: Key the cache on the path, not the name
stories.description: R12 and R13. The real tree has both collisions: two models sharing one stem in one folder, and two models sharing a basename in different folders.
stories.requirements: Path identity.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No model overwrites another's artifacts.
stories.qa_tests: Both collision shapes get their own mesh and thumbnail. Breaks if the key is the basename or the stem — and the real tree contains three files sharing the stem 2g-box-underdesk-v3.

stories.title: Never serve a half-written mesh
stories.description: R13. A mesh read while being written parses as a valid STL with geometry missing — it renders fine and is wrong, which is the opposite of what this page exists to do.
stories.requirements: Readiness is not inferred from the file existing.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The bytes route refuses while a build is in progress.
stories.qa_tests: Mid-build, the listing reports building and the bytes route refuses; after completion both succeed. Breaks if readiness is inferred from existence.

stories.title: Leave a source alone while it is still being written
stories.description: R13. A source read while Skippy rebuilds it tears the same way.
stories.requirements: Wait for the size to settle between two looks.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A changing source is not converted.
stories.qa_tests: A source whose size changes between looks is left alone until it settles. Breaks if the worker triggers on the first mtime change.

stories.title: Write conversions atomically so an interrupted build leaves no usable artifact
stories.requirements: Never write directly to the final path.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A killed build leaves the previous good mesh in place.
stories.qa_tests: A build killed part-way leaves the old mesh, and the next build replaces it whole. Breaks if conversion writes directly to the final path.

stories.title: Rebuild a changed source and leave an unchanged one alone
stories.description: R11 and R12.
stories.requirements: The key reflects content.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A rewrite produces a new mesh; a sweep over unchanged sources writes nothing.
stories.qa_tests: Both directions. Breaks if the key ignores content, or ignores it the other way.

stories.title: Make the five failure states distinguishable on one listing
stories.description: R14. Could not convert, could not be read, could not be pictured, still building, and timed out.
stories.requirements: Five distinct states, not a shared error.
stories.acceptance_criteria: One call over one fixture tree yields five different states.
stories.qa_tests: A garbage STEP, an unreadable file, a model whose render fails, a build in flight and a conversion that exceeded its timeout produce five states. Breaks if any two collapse into one — the single try/except that ruins this is one edit away.

stories.title: Abandon a conversion that hangs
stories.description: R14. Killed at the timeout and recorded as timed out.
stories.requirements: A hard timeout.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A converter that never returns does not stall the worker.
stories.qa_tests: A converter that never returns is killed and recorded. Breaks if there is no timeout — the test hangs rather than fails, which is the point.

stories.title: Treat a filename as data rather than syntax
stories.description: R28. The real tree has an apostrophe in a directory name.
stories.requirements: No string interpolation into a command.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A name with an apostrophe, a space and a quote converts and executes nothing.
stories.qa_tests: Breaks if the converter is driven by string interpolation.

features.title: The gallery
features.description: The site as a pure reader over the cache.
features.requirements: R1: a page showing every model file under the models tree as a gallery of cards. R2: a model file means STL, 3MF, OBJ, STEP, STP or FCStd matched regardless of letter case, so an uppercase extension appears, while FreeCAD backups, gcode, archives, images, drawings and scratch directories are not model files and get no card. R3: each card shows a small picture, the file name and the file size. R4: browsable by folder, each folder showing its own files and subfolders rather than one flat list of several hundred. R5: a folder that legitimately holds no models says it is empty, and a folder that cannot be read says it cannot be read — the two are never the same card. R15: if the models directory is absent, or present but unreadable, or mounted but empty because the mount failed, the gallery says which, and none of those is shown as a gallery with no models in it. R29: opening the gallery does not make one auth call per card.
features.acceptance_criteria: No absence is silent and no failure is shown as emptiness.
features.qa_tests: The mount-failed case is the one that cannot be caught by an existence check, because Docker creates a missing bind mount as an empty directory — so that is the one case that cannot occur in production and the check needs a sentinel instead.

stories.title: List models and only models, case-insensitively
stories.description: R1 and R2.
stories.requirements: Six extensions, any case. Backups, gcode, archives, images, drawings and scratch directories excluded.
stories.acceptance_criteria: An uppercase .STL appears; an .FCStd.bak-* does not.
stories.qa_tests: A fixture tree with four models plus an .FCBak, an .FCStd.bak-20260922-1928, a .gcode, a .png and a __pycache__ lists exactly the four. Breaks if matching is case-sensitive (the uppercase one vanishes) or prefix-based (the two backups appear).

stories.title: Report each file's real size
stories.requirements: Read from the file, not the cache record.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Exact bytes.
stories.qa_tests: A fixture of exactly 1234 bytes reports 1234. Breaks if rounded to kilobytes, or read from the cache record.

stories.title: List a folder's own contents rather than the whole tree
stories.description: R4. Several hundred models in one flat list is the failure.
stories.requirements: No recursion into a flat list.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A folder shows its files and its subfolders.
stories.qa_tests: A root with two models and a subfolder holding a third lists two models and one folder; the subfolder lists the third.

stories.title: Distinguish empty from unreadable
stories.requirements: PermissionError is never swallowed into an empty list.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Two different answers.
stories.qa_tests: An empty folder reports empty; one whose mode blocks listing reports unreadable. The real tree has a restrictive mode on the root itself.

stories.title: Distinguish absent, unreadable and mount-failed at the root
stories.requirements: A sentinel, because an existence check cannot tell mount-failed from empty — Docker creates a missing bind mount as an empty directory.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Three answers, none of them an empty gallery.
stories.qa_tests: A root that does not exist, one that cannot be listed, and one that exists and is empty but carries no sentinel each report differently. Breaks if the check is root.exists().

stories.title: Verify the session once per gallery, not once per card
stories.requirements: A verification cache.
stories.acceptance_criteria: One auth call for a folder of many models.
stories.qa_tests: Listing a folder of many models verifies the session once. Breaks if the verification cache is removed — the blocking httpx.get in auth_client.verify_token is a round trip per request.

features.title: The 3D view
features.description: What the browser does with a normalised binary STL.
features.requirements: R6: tapping a card opens that model in a 3D view. R7: the view orbits, pans and zooms by mouse on a desktop and by touch on a phone. R8: tapping a card opens the view immediately before anything downloads, and while the mesh downloads the view shows the word loading and then a counting percentage over the model area. R9: going back while a model is still downloading abandons the download and returns to the folder it came from. R21: a plane can be dragged through the model to cut it open and see inside. R22: when a model Daniel has open is rebuilt, the view swaps to the new version on its own within a second or two of the new mesh being ready, keeping the camera exactly where Daniel had it. R23: that automatic updating stops while the tab is not being looked at and resumes when it is. R35: the back button and the section slider belong to the 3D view and appear nowhere else.
features.acceptance_criteria: One loader, no text parsing, and no 179 MB OBJ opened in phone Safari.
features.qa_tests: Most of this is verified live at ship time rather than by the suite, because browser behaviour has no assertable surface in pytest — named here rather than covered by a test asserting something adjacent. The one assertable piece is the change signal.

stories.title: Open, orbit, pan and zoom by mouse and by touch
stories.description: R6 and R7.
stories.requirements: Both input modes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Works on a desktop and on a phone.
stories.qa_tests: Verified live at ship time by hand against the real page. No assertable surface in pytest.

stories.title: Open immediately with a loading percentage, and cancel on back
stories.description: R8 and R9. The view appears before anything downloads; the percentage counts over the model area; back abandons the download.
stories.requirements: The view opens first, the bytes follow.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Back returns immediately rather than waiting on the download.
stories.qa_tests: Verified live: the progress bar tracks a real download and the cancel returns immediately.

stories.title: Add a draggable section plane
stories.description: R21. Cut the model open and see inside.
stories.requirements: Dragged through the model.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The interior is visible.
stories.qa_tests: Verified live: the plane cuts the solid and reveals the interior.

stories.title: Swap in a rebuilt model keeping the camera still
stories.description: R22 and R23. Within a second or two of the new mesh being ready, with the camera exactly where Daniel had it. Polling stops while the tab is hidden.
stories.requirements: The change signal moves only when the mesh is ready.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The camera does not jump.
stories.qa_tests: The polled value changes after a rebuild completes and does not change while one is in flight. Breaks if it reports the source's mtime — which changes on the first byte written, not the last. The camera-held behaviour is verified live.

stories.title: Keep the back button and section slider inside the 3D view
stories.description: R35. They appear nowhere else.
stories.requirements: Scoped to the view.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The gallery carries neither.
stories.qa_tests: Verified by looking at the gallery. A panel carries labels rather than narration, so these controls belong where they act.

features.title: Skippy's camera control
features.description: The reason the page exists: both of them provably looking at the same feature.
features.requirements: R16: Skippy can put Daniel's open view on a specific spot on a specific model, and the view moves there without Daniel touching anything. R17: Skippy can place a marker on the model that Daniel can see, and a later camera push without a marker clears it rather than leaving a stale one. R18: when Daniel moves the view and stops, his position is reported back, and Skippy can ask where Daniel is looking. R19: an answer to where Daniel is looking says whether a browser has actually reported since Skippy's last push — Skippy is never handed his own pushed camera as though it were Daniel's. R20: two tabs open on one model do not fight each other for the camera.
features.acceptance_criteria: The subtlest finding in the review was Skippy reading his own push back as Daniel's answer: one slot, two writers, and a confident wrong answer.
features.qa_tests: A push and a report are different things, which means two slots rather than one. The echo-suppression test matters because without it two tabs oscillate once a second.

stories.title: Keep a push and a report in separate slots
stories.description: R16, R18 and R19. One slot with two writers is how Skippy reads his own push back as confirmation.
stories.requirements: A read says whether a browser has actually reported since the last push.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Skippy is never handed his own push as Daniel's.
stories.qa_tests: After a push with no browser report, a read says so and does not return the pushed value. After a browser reports, the read returns the browser's. Breaks if one slot holds both.

stories.title: Keep cameras per model
stories.requirements: Not one global camera.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A camera pushed for one model is not returned for another.
stories.qa_tests: Breaks if there is one global camera.

stories.title: Clear a marker on a push that carries none
stories.description: R17. A stale marker is worse than no marker, because it points at the wrong thing confidently.
stories.requirements: Markers travel with the camera push rather than being stored separately.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A later push without a marker returns no marker.
stories.qa_tests: A push carrying a marker returns it; a later push without one returns none. Breaks if markers are stored separately and never cleared.

stories.title: Suppress a tab's own echo so two tabs do not fight
stories.requirements: A camera carrying a writer identity is not handed back to that writer as something to move to.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Two tabs on one model are stable.
stories.qa_tests: A camera carrying a writer identity is not returned to that writer. Breaks if echo suppression is dropped — two tabs then oscillate once a second.

features.title: Auth and containment
features.description: Only Daniel, logged into the site, sees any of it; Skippy reaches it with his own token.
features.requirements: R24: every route is covered, including the ones that serve file bytes. R25: with no token configured, no bearer gets in — including an empty one — while Daniel's login still works, because the token is Skippy's way in rather than his. R26: a credential that is not valid is refused as unauthorised and never as a server error, whatever bytes it contains. R27: nothing outside the models directory and the cache is reachable through the viewer, including via a symlink pointing out of either.
features.acceptance_criteria: Eleven of the original twenty-one tests passed against the bug they named, and the worst was here: 'no token configured authorizes nobody' only failed for an empty presented bearer, which the original test never sent.
features.qa_tests: A per-route table is the only shape that catches a guard dropped from one route. The non-ASCII bearer test exists because compare_digest raises TypeError on a str holding anything outside ASCII, and the route then answers 500 — which reads as 'the site is down' rather than as a refused credential.

stories.title: Guard every route, bytes routes included
stories.requirements: A per-route table, not a sample.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No route is reachable without a credential.
stories.qa_tests: A table of every route in the feature, each refused with no credential and each accepted with Daniel's cookie. Breaks if the guard is dropped from any one of them — a per-route table is the only shape that catches it.

stories.title: Admit no bearer when no token is configured
stories.description: R25. The configured token swept over unset, empty and whitespace, and the presented bearer over absent, empty and wrong.
stories.requirements: Every combination refused, while Daniel's cookie still gets in.
stories.acceptance_criteria: An unconfigured token locks the bearer path rather than opening it.
stories.qa_tests: All nine combinations refused. Breaks if an empty configured token compares equal to an empty header — which is exactly what the original test failed to send.

stories.title: Refuse an uncomparable credential as 401 rather than 500
stories.requirements: Compare as bytes.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A refusal reads as a refusal.
stories.qa_tests: A bearer carrying non-ASCII bytes is refused as unauthorised. Breaks if comparison is done on str — compare_digest raises TypeError and the route answers 500, which reads as 'the site is down' and sends the operator to the wrong remedy.

stories.title: Judge containment on the resolved path
stories.description: R27. The models tree carries symlinks legitimately.
stories.requirements: Resolved, not lexical.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A symlink pointing out of the tree is refused.
stories.qa_tests: A path climbing out is refused; a symlink inside the tree pointing outside is refused; an ordinary nested file is served. Breaks if the check is lexical — the symlink case is what catches it.

features.title: Addresses and history
features.description: So a link opens where it says it does.
features.requirements: R31: every folder has its own web address at any depth, and an open model is that folder's address with the model named as a query parameter. R32: moving into a folder and opening a model each add exactly one browser history entry — back goes exactly one step and forward returns. R33: back from the address the user arrived at directly leaves the models section rather than walking the gallery backwards. R34: reloading any of these addresses restores what was on screen, including after a session has lapsed and been logged in again. R36: an address naming a folder that does not exist corrects itself to the models root with a note, one naming a model that does not exist corrects itself to that model's folder with a note, and a models directory that is missing or unreadable says so and keeps the address, because the remedy is a mount rather than a different folder.
features.acceptance_criteria: A shared link opens the thing it names, and back behaves the way a browser user expects.
features.qa_tests: R36's third case is the one that distinguishes a correction from a diagnosis: a bad folder is corrected, but a broken mount keeps its address because changing it would hide the real problem.

stories.title: Give every folder its own address and name an open model as a query parameter
stories.description: R31, at any depth.
stories.requirements: Addressable at any depth.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A link opens where it says it does.
stories.qa_tests: A deep folder's address opens that folder. A model-naming address opens that model in that folder.

stories.title: Add exactly one history entry per navigation
stories.description: R32 and R33. Back goes one step, forward returns, and back from a direct arrival leaves the section.
stories.requirements: One entry per navigation, not one per render.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Back does not walk the gallery backwards from a direct arrival.
stories.qa_tests: Entering a folder and opening a model each add one entry. Back from the arrival address leaves the models section.

stories.title: Restore state on reload, including across a lapsed session
stories.requirements: Survives a re-login.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A reload shows what was on screen.
stories.qa_tests: Reloading a folder address and a model address each restore. After a session lapses and is logged in again, the same addresses restore rather than landing on a root.

stories.title: Correct a bad address with a note, but keep it when the mount is broken
stories.description: R36. A missing folder corrects to the root; a missing model corrects to its folder; a missing or unreadable models directory says so and keeps the address, because the remedy is a mount rather than a different folder.
stories.requirements: Three behaviours, the third deliberately different.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A broken mount is diagnosed rather than papered over.
stories.qa_tests: Each of the three cases behaves distinctly. The third is what separates a correction from a diagnosis — redirecting on a broken mount would hide it.

features.title: Test hygiene for this change
features.description: Existing tests deleted as part of this change, for failing the standard, in files this change touches.
features.requirements: Deleted: test_home_dashboard_shows_all_link_groups, test_grafana_link_is_tls, test_nav_groups_sites_and_homelab_dropdowns and test_health, all of which asserted constants against themselves or were self-evident; test_btc_page_renders_for_authed_user, a spellchecker; and test_api_btc_stats_proxies_ledger and test_api_btc_observations_proxies_ledger, which patch the very function whose proxying is under test.
features.acceptance_criteria: A test that cannot fail against any implementation is deleted on sight rather than kept for coverage.
features.qa_tests: The rule being applied: a test may only be written where code external to the test decides whether it passes. A test that patches the function under test, or asserts a constant against itself, is banned outright.

stories.title: Delete the seven tests that cannot fail
stories.description: Four asserting constants against themselves or self-evident facts, one spellchecker, and two patching the function whose behaviour they claim to test.
stories.requirements: Deleted rather than rewritten, where the behaviour is already covered or not worth covering.
stories.acceptance_criteria: No remaining test in these files passes regardless of implementation.
stories.qa_tests: Each deletion is justified by the standard: if no edit outside the test file can change its outcome, it is banned outright.
